Priya (CSM): Heads up — during Aperture's onboarding ramp this morning we saw p95 latency jump to ~2.8s and a small uptick in 5xxs around 09:12 PST. Not consistent but correlated with spike in long-context requests.
Kevin (ML Eng): Thanks, good catch. Is there a sample request or trace we can look at? long-context as in >1024 tokens?
Priya (CSM): Yes, sent trace link in DM (redwood://trace/aps-2026-03-22/894). Most requests are chat completions with 1.2k-2k tokens prefix.
Sam (Platform Eng): Pattern makes sense — KV cache miss due to varying prefixes. Quick mitigation: route heavy long-context traffic to compact-xxl-int8 for those users and warm KV cache for session-based flows. We can add a per-customer routing tag.
Lena (AE): Any risk to response quality if we swap to int8 compact? Renewal convo coming up next week, want to avoid regressions.
Kevin (ML Eng): Short answer: small risk. Recommendation: staged A/B canary — 10% traffic to compact-int8 with identical prompts, collect quality signals (ROUGE/QA accuracy + manual eval on 200 prompt pairs). If quality delta <= 1.5% we proceed. Also enable fallback to baseline model on low-confidence outputs (score < 0.65).
Priya (CSM): Sounds good. Can we make the routing change reversible quickly? Customer is sensitive.
Sam (Platform Eng): Yes — we'll implement a dynamic routing rule tied to customer_id and can flip in Console (per-route toggle). Snippet for the rule we plan to apply:
```
route_rule:
  match: "customer_id:aperture"
  variants:
    - model: "redwood/compact-xxl-int8"
      weight: 10
    - model: "redwood/standard-xxl"
      weight: 90
  fallback: "redwood/standard-xxl"
  metrics: ["p50_latency","p95_latency","error_rate","quality_delta"]
```
Priya (CSM): Nice. What telemetry will we need for the QE checks?
Kevin (ML Eng): Collect token-level cost, latency (p50/p95), rerank/QA accuracy on the eval set, hallucination flags from the eval harness, and output log probability to compute confidence. I'll attach a 200-prompt eval set to the ticket.
Sam (Platform Eng): I'll create the canary with 10% split, KV cache prewarm for active sessions, and add a circuit-breaker that auto-rolls back on >1% 5xx or p95 > 3.5s for 10m.
Lena (AE): Please tag me on the rollout so I can update Aperture before the call. If quality holds we'll position this as cost-lowering optimization.
ops-bot: deploy-canary created: canary-aps-4167890123 (10%): https://console.redwood/inference/canaries/canary-aps-4167890123
Priya (CSM): Action items: Kevin -> upload eval set + target metrics, Sam -> create routing rule + canary and circuit-breaker, Kevin+Priya -> schedule quick smoke + manual eval in 48h, Lena -> prep renewal note. Anyone else?
Kevin (ML Eng): I'll also add a short test that replays 100 recent requests with full context to check cache warmup behavior.
Sam (Platform Eng): I'll instrument a dashboard with these KPIs and add an alert to #eng-oncall if circuit trips.
Lena (AE): Thx team — please keep updates minimal in this thread, I'll consolidate for the renewal brief. :thumbsup:
Priya (CSM): Rolling this out to the canary now. Will post first 1h telemetry snapshot in ~60m.
ops-bot: telemetry snapshot scheduled at +60m for canary-aps-4167890123
Priya (CSM): (follow-up) 1h snapshot: p95 down to 1.1s on canary, no uplift in 5xx, initial quality delta 0.6% (Kevin to confirm). Looks promising.
Kevin (ML Eng): Confirmed — quality delta on 200 eval prompts = 0.64% lower on compact-int8, confidence distribution similar. Recommend continue ramp to 30% and re-evaluate.
Sam (Platform Eng): Ramp to 30% now, route updated. Will watch for anomalies.
Lena (AE): Great — I'll update Aperture and note potential 18% cost savings if finalized.
Priya (CSM): Thanks all. Will update renewal tracker and close this ticket after 72h stable.
